extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship 2026 (prospective URF applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship 2026, covering eligibility, application form completion, supporting documents, budgets, and feedback policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent fellowship applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I apply for other fellowships at the same time as the University Research Fellowship?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes, this is possible as we understand that researchers might apply for other opportunities at the same time as the University Research Fellowship. Please include any active fellowship applications in the “Applicant Research Funding” question of the application form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of accepting permanent post during assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: If I accept a permanent position or equivalent fellowship during the URF assessment, how is my application affected?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must remain eligible until the time of the application deadline. If you accept a permanent post or equivalent fellowship after the application deadline, this will not preclude you from staying in the competition. If invited to interview, you can include this as part of your updates since submission. If offered a URF award, you would be required to resign from the position or equivalent fellowship to be able to accept the URF offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes, as long as an applicant continues to meet the eligibility criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: COVID-19 impact reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: How will the Royal Society consider the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic on my application?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Royal Society has a specific question in the application form for applicants to outline the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on their research. Applicants should use that question to describe complex/varied impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget period and costing
rubrics_metrics.description: How many years should costs be provided for in the application form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please provide costs for all 8 years of the fellowship. When completing the budget table in Flexi-Grant® please ensure to provide values at cost, including inflation if appropriate. For more information, see the Royal Society Grant Funding Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research proposal page limit (images & references)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do images and references need to be included within the four-page limit of the research proposal or are they in addition to?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All images and references have to fit within the four-page limit of the research proposal document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications list guidance and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot fit all of my publications in the application due to the word limit. Which ones should I include?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please include your most relevant publications (up to 20). If you are the first author, you can add ‘et al’ while if you are not the first author, you can include the initials for all contributing. Reviewers will be able to see the full list of your publications through your ORCID ID, which is part of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission completeness requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: I have completed all the sections and the application is at 100% but I cannot see a button to submit my application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All participants on the participants tab must appear as ‘complete’ in green before the submit button appears. If a participant appears in orange as ‘incomplete’ they need to login and select ‘Save & Submit’ on the application form page or ‘Submit your contribution’ on the summary page – otherwise you will not be able to submit your application to your host institution for approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required letters of support
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of supports from the Head of Department and Nominated Referee are compulsory, while the Research Support is optional and can be revoked if no longer needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head of Department contributions (statement and resources)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the Head of Department expected to contribute to the application form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Head of Department section comprises two parts: (1) Statement of Support (PDF upload) — further guidance provided within the scheme notes for the round; and (2) Commitment of Resources (max 250 words text box) — provide details of the resources that the department will commit to the applicant. This section will be included in the award letter if the application is successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback availability and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Can I request feedback on my University Research Fellowship application?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to the high volume of applications, the Society cannot provide feedback for applications unsuccessful at the first Panel assessment stage. Applicants can request feedback if their application has completed the independent peer review assessment stage. Details of how to request feedback will be provided when applicants are notified about the status of their application.
